ring_road_entry.speaker: narrator
ring_road_entry.text: Three days after the court's seventh-day review, spring sunlight opens a road through the rain. Wei Jin waits with a sounding pole and ropes. Su Lan carries Wei Xiu's morning notes; she has offered assistance for this afternoon alone. The third ring remains sealed with the Mooring Eel. Lin Yue feels the pendant warm against her ribs as she approaches. Today she has agreed to walk one road, hear one person's account, and return with questions that the other investigators can answer beside their own evidence. Wei Jin unrolls his daughter's map before anyone steps downhill.

ring_road_waterline.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_waterline.text: This used to be the shorter approach. A farmer could bring a basket here without paying a cart to go round the bend. Last winter's water left timber across the ditch, and this morning Xiu heard the old mooring groan. We closed the track before anyone came with a load. I asked you because a sword can reach a rope that a pole cannot. I did not ask you to make the crossing safe by looking heroic. If we fail, the track stays closed and the baskets take the longer road.

ring_road_daughter.speaker: su_lan
ring_road_daughter.text: Xiu left these notes after this morning's survey. The abandoned berth is above the vanished east stair, with a drainage channel between them. She marked firm ground on the high path and found a hollow beneath the platform's downstream corner. Wei Jin will lead our work. I can keep his warning cords visible, read the measurements, and call a change before either of you moves. I maintain bell ropes; I have enough respect for a strained line to watch it closely. A ferryman's map is useful only while we remember who measured it and when.

ring_road_fare.speaker: narrator
ring_road_fare.text: At the road's first turn, a woman settles two salt baskets beneath an awning and starts the longer walk without them. Wei Jin calls the carrier on the public route, arranging a place on the afternoon cart. The fee comes from his own purse. The woman thanks him for a service, then asks when she may collect the baskets. He cannot promise a reopening. Lin Yue notices the difference between the copper he can spend and the assurance he cannot honestly sell. They cover the baskets and leave her a written collection time.

ring_road_approach.speaker: narrator
ring_road_approach.text: The disused approach narrows between reed beds. Flood mud clings to the stems halfway up their height, though new leaves have pushed beyond it. Wei Jin strikes each paving stone with his pole before he steps. Ahead, a square mooring block leans over the drainage cut. A whole willow trunk has lodged beneath its fallen retaining rope. Every pulse of water lifts the trunk a finger's width. Then it settles, dragging the rope tighter. Something deep inside the bank clicks with the patient regularity of a tooth working loose from its gum.

ring_road_permit_question.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_permit_question.text: Before we start, I want to keep the two questions apart. This road needs work whether the ring belongs to you or someone else. You can decline to talk about your old permit and still ask me to cut a dangerous line. If you do talk, I will bring only the details you offer to the common meeting. An Ru and the Eel's investigator are taking their own roads. I will not borrow their conclusions in advance. A resemblance may give us a reason to compare evidence; it cannot supply the comparison itself.

ring_road_closed_ground.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_closed_ground.text: Then leave your questions in your pocket until we have a place to stand. See those pale stones? They look dry because the sun reaches them. The water has eaten underneath. I knew a man who judged a bank by the dust on top and spent the next month learning to walk again. He lived, which made his neighbors call the accident fortunate while his wife carried every sack. We put our ropes on the inland posts. Lan marks the margin I choose. You step back when either of us calls, however steady your qi feels.

ring_road_soundings.speaker: narrator
ring_road_soundings.text: Wei Jin checked the inland stones against his daughter's notes and lowered the sounding pole without leaning over the cut. It found a hollow beneath the missing step. Su Lan marked a red margin. Lin Yue kept her field closed. She could hear the water and feel ordinary vibration through firm paving; she could not send qi down unopened leg meridians or sense a hidden foundation. She placed her feet where the ferryman's pole found support and accepted the free rope tail.

ring_road_first_rope.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_first_rope.text: This rope belongs to the current landing store. It is sound, and I will record any damage before it goes back. The dark rope on the willow belongs to the abandoned mooring. That one has spent the winter alternately wet and freezing. We do not pull against it. We catch the trunk with ours, take the strain on the inland posts, and cut the old line where you can reach it from the marked ground. If the trunk turns toward the bank instead of the drainage mouth, let your blade fall away and call it.

ring_road_timber_warning.speaker: narrator
ring_road_timber_warning.text: A wave catches under the willow's split crown. One bare branch rises like a hand, striking the mooring block with a flat crack. Gravel spills into the ditch. Lin Yue pulls her sword clear by instinct, then holds the point down. The cutting place has shifted beyond her safe reach. Wei Jin calls a retreat. Su Lan lifts the red cord farther inland, leaving nobody between it and the water. They wait for the branch to settle. The old rope draws another thread from its fraying middle, and a brown splinter lands beside Wei Jin's boot.

ring_road_brace_choice.speaker: su_lan
ring_road_brace_choice.text: The trunk is still caught. We have time to improve one part of our preparation before we take its weight. You can help Wei Jin spread the load between the inland posts, or help me mark the likely swing of the broken crown. We will finish the other task while you work. Both jobs matter; neither buys permission to cross the red cord. Choose where your hands will be useful. Wei Jin will call the start. A flooded path has room for patience, even when the wood sounds as though it disagrees. I will watch his signals.

choices.text: Spread the anchor load with Wei Jin.
Mark the willow crown's likely swing with Su Lan.

ring_road_brace_bank.speaker: narrator
ring_road_brace_bank.text: Wei Jin showed Lin Yue the two inland posts and their padded guides. She carried slack line to the second guide on firm ground while he retained control. Neither person became a body anchor. She checked the angle against Su Lan's mark and reported a chafing edge before any load transfer. Jin adjusted the ordinary padding, then returned the rope to its rated path. Yue's field stayed closed. The preparation improved their rig and her understanding of it; it taught no new qi technique.

ring_road_brace_angle.speaker: narrator
ring_road_brace_angle.text: Lin Yue follows the crown's outline with her eyes while Su Lan holds the pole along its visible length. A forked branch could sweep uphill if the trunk rolls. They place two cords beyond its longest reach, making a second margin visible from the posts. Wei Jin finishes padding the anchors, then asks Su Lan to check his knots against her bell-rope practice. She does so without ceremony. Lin Yue studies the new boundary until she could find it through rain. Having drawn the danger on the ground, she feels less tempted to imagine herself faster than it.

ring_road_anchor.speaker: narrator
ring_road_anchor.text: Their new rope slips beneath the willow on a pole, then comes back over its narrower end. Wei Jin coaxes the loop into a natural fork with short movements rather than a hard pull. Lin Yue feeds him slack from the inland side. Su Lan watches the block and calls each change in its lean. When the rope finally sits, the three stop speaking for a breath. A kingfisher flashes across the far reeds. Water takes up the unfinished noise beneath them. Wei Jin lifts his empty hand, and they begin taking the weight together.

ring_road_listen_load.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_listen_load.text: Feel that? A rope talks before it fails. There is the pull of the trunk, and there is the scrape where it has found an edge. Keep your hands clear of the bite. If you wrap it round your wrist, the river can take your arm as a handle. I have watched cultivators do that because they trusted their bones more than the hemp. Perhaps their bones survived. The shore people still had to cut them loose. Set your strength where it can leave the job when we need it to leave.

ring_road_qi_limit.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_qi_limit.text: My first pair permits a stopped small pulse. It does not let me brace a whole willow with my legs or hold a changing load indefinitely. Keep the weight on your tested posts and rope guides. I can handle the free control tail from firm ground and release it when you call. My field stays closed for this long task. If the guide cannot carry the load, we stop; my body will not be its hidden replacement anchor.

ring_road_sword_cut.speaker: narrator
ring_road_sword_cut.text: The new line settled against the padded posts and guides. Wei Jin indicated a slack span of old hemp within the marked reach. Lin Yue kept her first pair closed. The ordinary sharpened blade cut slack fibers; no qi edge, aura or core technique appeared. She stayed on firm ground, clear of the new rope and the trunk. The severed length fell into the ditch. As the other end snapped against the block, she lowered the blade rather than following it into the changing load.

ring_road_splinter.speaker: narrator
ring_road_splinter.text: Then the split crown twists. A hidden branch catches the drainage lip, and the rope in Wei Jin's hands gives a sharp sideways jump. He lets it run through the guide instead of trying to catch it bare. A splinter bursts from the rotten mooring face, hitting Lin Yue's sleeve. She feels cloth tear and turns her forearm away. The blade drops to her side, well clear of the load. Su Lan calls for stillness. Below them, the crown is pinned again, its newly exposed branch pointing directly toward the lowest anchor rope.

ring_road_rollback.speaker: su_lan
ring_road_rollback.text: Nobody pull. The branch will cut our line if we drag it uphill. Jin, keep what weight you have without adding any. Yue, lay your sword on the dry stones and move behind the second cord. Jin has seen the hollow widen and called a new margin; I will mark it before we move. You can be angry with the lost time afterward. Right now I would rather bring home an unfinished road than explain why a person was standing on ground our ferryman had already told them could give way. Let him choose our next move.

ring_road_pole.speaker: narrator
ring_road_pole.text: Lin Yue obeys, though her pulse urges one more quick cut. From behind the second cord she sees what impatience had hidden: the bank beneath her former place has cracked from end to end. At Wei Jin's direction, Su Lan lays a spare pole across the forked branch, guiding its point away from their rope. The pole bends before the branch moves. Wei Jin eases the load by a handspan. Water lifts the trunk, releasing pressure. Lan draws her pole back whole. The crown swings into the channel, close enough to throw cold spray over their boots.

ring_road_wet_stone.speaker: narrator
ring_road_wet_stone.text: The abandoned platform folded into the water. Its lowest stones vanished; paving tilted above exposed willow roots. Lin Yue stepped farther inland with her field closed. Wei Jin shifted the working rope through its guides onto the surviving posts; she handled only its unloaded control tail. Her forearm stung beneath a torn sleeve. Across the ditch, the trunk rolled clear of the block. Su Lan watched its next possible catch. The strengthened posts, rather than a novice's untested stance, still bore the load.

ring_road_vow.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_vow.text: My sword vow sounded grand when I first spoke it on the mountain. Here it has become a rather ordinary instruction: do not make somebody carry the price of my haste. I saw the loose branch and wanted to finish the cut before it could move. Jin saw the ground beneath me. We needed both kinds of seeing, but his had to come first. My teacher used to say a sharp blade makes every knot look impatient. I thought he meant children. I am beginning to suspect he meant swordspeople of every age.

ring_road_release.speaker: narrator
ring_road_release.text: Su Lan counted the water pulses while Wei Jin watched the trunk turn toward the open ditch. At his signal, Lin Yue paid out the free control tail through the guide from firm ground. The posts and rig carried the weight; no sustained qi or body anchor held it. They let the crown pass without scraping the surviving posts. Wei Jin released the loop with his pole. The rope returned empty, and Lan marked the downstream debris bed for the next ordinary survey.

ring_road_wake.speaker: narrator
ring_road_wake.text: Water rushes through the unblocked ditch. It carries pale chips, an old leaf basket, and the bitter smell of mud that has lain covered all winter. Lin Yue's muscles release their held tension in uneven waves. The bank remains broken. Nothing in the successful cut has made the abandoned berth fit for boats. Wei Jin tests the inland posts after unloading them and finds one loosened socket. He ties a warning cord round it. The three stand well back as the fresh flow settles, listening for another buried piece of timber against the stones.

ring_road_detour.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_detour.text: We have cleared a threat to the upper path, but we have found more damage than the morning notes showed. I am keeping the lower approach shut. The baskets use the long road this evening and the boat uses the current public landing. Lan, I know you remember this path before every spring became a new detour. I remember it too. My notice goes to the crews before my hopes do. We can ask for a repair survey tomorrow, with actual labor and material prices beside the map. Xiu will need the new measurements before making her own plans.

ring_road_drain.speaker: narrator
ring_road_drain.text: They recover the guide slings from firm ground and examine every wet length of rope. One carries a roughened patch where the branch grazed it. Wei Jin marks that part with a white tie so nobody returns it to service by mistake. The sun has moved beyond the willow tops, leaving the ditch in shade. A reed warbler starts its spring call from the far bank. Lin Yue wants to sit in the grass and let the sound replace the working rhythm in her head. Instead she helps carry the damaged rope to the high path.

ring_road_no_passage.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_no_passage.text: I used to tell passengers this approach was easy because I could walk it with my eyes half shut. Then I learned how much easier it became when someone else brought the baskets. We will put a notice where the road divides, before a traveler has paid to bring a load this far. Lan can write the changed route. I will speak to the carrier about two extra cart turns. A closed road costs real money. Leaving people to discover the closure at its end costs the same money, plus the strength they have already spent.

ring_road_costs.speaker: narrator
ring_road_costs.text: At the ticket house, Wei Jin lays the damaged rope on the counter and pays for its replacement from his repair purse. The clerk gives a receipt for the rope alone. The cart carrier has another price for the extra turns, and Wei Jin writes that separately. Lin Yue watches two problems acquire two clear costs. An immortal could stand at the ditch for a season, holding the willow in place by force of will. It would still leave the salt baskets under an awning, waiting for a person whose afternoon had already been spent.

ring_road_wage.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_wage.text: Do not turn that look into an offer to pay for everything, Yue. You gave us an afternoon's work, and I am grateful. The landing needs a repair account it can use after you have gone. I can cover today's rope and these cart turns. Tomorrow's survey belongs before the crews, with whoever owns the damaged ground. We must show the people paying what the job actually needs. A purse opened out of kindness can hide a missing plan. I want both the kindness and the plan, written where neither can swallow the other.

ring_road_injury.speaker: narrator
ring_road_injury.text: Su Lan catches Lin Yue rubbing her forearm and asks to see it. Beneath the torn sleeve, the splinter has left a shallow cut with a brown fragment still caught at one end. They wash the skin, remove the visible fragment, and bind the cut with clean cloth. Lin Yue's qi has already quieted; the arm remains sore. She agrees to have the wound checked if pain, swelling, or heat increases. Wei Jin sets her share of the wet rope aside. Their conversation waits while ordinary water and a bandage do their necessary work.

ring_road_tea.speaker: narrator
ring_road_tea.text: The kettle in the ticket house smells faintly of toasted rice. Su Lan pours herself a cup and gives the warmer one to Lin Yue without making a lesson of it. Wei Jin sits facing the road where the carrier will arrive. His breathing has slowed, but his fingers tap against his knee whenever the ditch makes a loud splash beyond the wall. Lin Yue keeps her questions folded beside her cup. They discuss the salt baskets, the cart's wheel, and where the next notice should be hung so that rain will leave it readable.

ring_road_hands.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_hands.text: My hands do that after a hard pull. They tremble once the work has stopped. I can still tie a serviceable knot, though Lan checked today's and I let her. Thirty years carrying the same families teaches a man to recognize every shore face. It also teaches his daughter which tasks he pretends have stayed easy. You need not make an omen of the shaking. It tells you I held a rope this afternoon and must rest before holding another. Whatever the old receipt proves, it will not give these fingers back their first spring.

ring_road_older_crossing.speaker: narrator
ring_road_older_crossing.text: He turns his cup a quarter circle. A pale ring on the wood records the place where other cups have cooled during earlier floods. Lin Yue remembers his grandmother's signature on the common-water line and the living crews who had to decide what to do with it. Now Wei Jin is deciding what he himself will place on this table. Su Lan glances at the oilcloth bundle near his feet but does not reach for it. Outside, the carrier arrives. They settle the cart turns first, giving the ordinary business its own uninterrupted ending.

ring_road_alias.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_alias.text: Jin of the Lower Reed was the name on my first surviving permit. People called me that because the lower reed bed was where I kept my boat. I knew I was Wei Jin before a clerk put either name on bamboo. I know it now. When the charter line was suppressed, the public account stopped making room for that working name. My neighbors did not become strangers to me. But a passenger looking for an old receipt could follow the written name and find a blank place where a ferryman ought to answer.

ring_road_suppression.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_suppression.text: Then we should ask what the paper lost, without claiming you lost yourself. I have watched a tidy register make living households seem absent. A charter can do quieter harm: it can remove the path by which an old promise reaches its holder. If we find that path, you still decide what to do with the promise. Nobody can say that a corrected line gives them your whole account. I will put your present name beside the offered alias and say you supplied the connection. That tells the meeting who is speaking, and how we learned it.

ring_road_permit_offer.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_permit_offer.text: You may examine the permit itself. I keep it in the outer pocket of the roll, where the tools cannot scratch its face. Read the working name, number, and surviving shore mark. You may copy those details for the common meeting, and Lan may check your copy. Leave the folded paper inside the inner sleeve closed. It has a separate cover and a separate purpose. Offering one object from this bundle does not offer every object beside it. I will tell you what the other cover is when I have held the permit in my own hands again.

ring_road_permit_face.speaker: narrator
ring_road_permit_face.text: Wei Jin slides a thin bamboo permit out of its oilcloth pocket and places it where the window gives light. Its corners have worn round from handling. A cord hole near the top has been reinforced with a narrow brass eye. Lin Yue turns it only after he nods. One face carries the old working name; the reverse bears a landing mark, rubbed pale along its outer stroke. She draws both surfaces at their actual size. Su Lan points out a crack that could be mistaken for another character, and the copy records the crack as damage.

ring_road_serial.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_serial.text: I can read LR-6 beside Jin of the Lower Reed. The lower edge has a worn renewal notch and a chipped corner; I have drawn those too. This shows that you hold an old permit bearing that name and number, and you have stated that it was yours. It gives the other investigators details they can compare with sources they are allowed to consult. I cannot tell from this bamboo who deposited the third echo or what they deposited. I will keep that limit beside the drawing, so the number does not arrive at the meeting wearing a conclusion.

ring_road_expiry.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_expiry.text: The permit stopped governing my work long ago. Do not use it to charge a fare or claim that the abandoned berth may open. We use the current route notices for that. I kept this because it was the first written thing that called my boat a service rather than a favor. Years later the same office had fewer places for the people I carried. I can value the old bamboo without calling its clerks wise. Put that in your understanding if it helps; the comparison only needs the marks, my present statement, and the other sources.

ring_road_tool_roll.speaker: narrator
ring_road_tool_roll.text: He takes the permit back, then loosens the outer tie of his tool roll. An awl, a short bone needle, and a wooden toggle lie in separate channels of faded cloth. The awl's handle fits a hollow worn by his thumb. Inside the roll sits a small closed receipt cover, its cord still tied. Wei Jin sets that cover aside without undoing it. He spreads the empty cloth beneath the window. One edge has a doubled fold held by two short stitches. Lin Yue waits with her pencil above the paper, asking through stillness what he intends to offer.

ring_road_wrapping_offer.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_wrapping_offer.text: You may inspect this wrapping and draw its seam. I made it myself, and I am choosing to tell you where else I used that fold. The cover beside it stays tied. You may read the mark on its outside when I turn that face toward you, but the paper inside is a different offer for a different room. I would like Xiu present when we discuss it. She has heard my stories for years. Sometimes she remembers which part I claimed to see and which part somebody else told me after the weather had passed.

ring_road_fold.speaker: narrator
ring_road_fold.text: Wei Jin folds a clean scrap to show the movement without disturbing the old cloth. He turns one edge inward, then reverses the long fold beneath it, making a soft channel rather than a hard ridge. Two short stitches catch across the doubled section. The needle enters where a wooden toggle would bear on the cloth. Lin Yue draws the layers separately before she draws them closed. Su Lan checks which line lies above the other. The demonstration is small enough to fit beside a tea cup, yet his hands become steadier while they know exactly what to do.

ring_road_loop.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_loop.text: A retaining loop can wear through its own sleeve if you pull it over a rough edge. I used this fold once beside the old keeper's ferry, when a bronze loop bit its cloth guard. She gave me the loose sleeve to mend while she dealt with a passenger's receipt. I laid the long fold backward and caught it with two short stitches. I remember because she teased me for making a stitch shorter than my thumbnail. That is my recollection of work I did. The drawing shows how I still do it, not who holds any particular ring.

ring_road_repair.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_repair.text: Was the keeper asking you to handle an echo while you repaired the guard? I need the answer in the account, because a listener might hear the word loop and imagine that a seam gave you access to everything it held. If your hands worked on the cloth, I will say cloth. If somebody else supplied the passenger's details, I will say those were somebody else's words. The meeting may compare a repair description with permitted exterior evidence. It must not treat a useful craftsman's touch as permission to enter a confidence he was never offered.

ring_road_seam.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_seam.text: Only the loose cloth sleeve was on my knee. The keeper had separated it from the loop before she gave it to me. I did not handle the ring or listen to anybody's echo. I heard her thank me when I returned the guard, and I saw her put it aside for fitting. That is where my own sight ends. Write the seam as two short stitches across one long reverse fold. Another person could use it, or learn it by watching. It is a habit worth comparing, not a secret signature nobody else can make.

ring_road_craft.speaker: su_lan
ring_road_craft.text: I have used a similar fold to protect a bell cord from its guide. That does not make me the owner of a ferryman's echo. A practiced repair can travel between workshops; it is useful precisely because somebody else can learn it. The old wrapping has wear, but wear only tells us that cloth has been used. Put my observation beside Jin's demonstration. You can also say I watched you draw the permit he voluntarily offered today. I have not visited the archive or seen the Eel's token. Those comparisons belong to the people who did.

ring_road_copy.speaker: narrator
ring_road_copy.text: Lin Yue writes the seam description beneath three small drawings: the open fold, the closed fold, and the two crossing stitches. She labels the diagram as Wei Jin's demonstration with fresh cloth. Next comes a sketch of the old wrapping, including its frayed end and the narrow stain beside the awl pocket. Nothing has been cut from it. Wei Jin reads the labels aloud and corrects the word knot to stitch. Su Lan checks the correction. The page grows less elegant as every offered distinction acquires space, but much easier for an absent reader to question accurately.

ring_road_past_storm.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_past_storm.text: I remember sitting beneath the shelter while the keeper finished her papers. Rain fell from one broken corner of the roof into a bowl. A child on the public boat kept counting the drops as if numbers could make the crossing hurry. That afternoon was ordinary until I decided to leave a copy of something with the keeper. The original remained with me. I have never needed a ring to recognize the sound in my own head. The road back to that decision has been harder than the decision itself, partly because the written working name stopped answering travelers.

ring_road_deposit_limit.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_deposit_limit.text: I will record that you recall making a voluntary deposit, without adding what you deposited or declaring that it must be the unidentified ring. The missing page means we need a connection between your account and the Eel's particular custody record. Your permit and repair recollection help frame the comparison. The closed cover may provide another source if you choose to offer its contents later. For now its outside is the only part offered. An investigation can carry a promising question across a room without pretending the question has already become an answer just because somebody hopes it will.

ring_road_echo_difference.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_echo_difference.text: Yes. I left an external copy with her. I did not give away my mind, my name, or a piece that I need returned to become myself. I can still remember what I chose to preserve. If the copy survives, I may wish to receive it. I may wish to keep it sealed. Those are decisions I have not made today. You can put my words before the others, but do not summon a recovered man into your story. I am sitting here with tea on my sleeve and a road repair still waiting for tomorrow's prices.

ring_road_fear.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_fear.text: I was afraid the old alias would turn me into a curiosity at the meeting. A man whose name had vanished from one line would be invited to tell every sorrow he ever carried. People are generous with a witness while he makes their case feel complete. Then he asks for a cart, or says his hands are tired, and the generosity acquires conditions. I know these people better than that fear allows. Still, knowing does not make the fear disappear. I want to arrive with permission already drawn narrowly enough that I can breathe inside it.

ring_road_daughter_account.speaker: su_lan
ring_road_daughter_account.text: I can sit beside you without answering for you. I can remind you which paper you offered. When Xiu returns from the marsh, she can join us before you decide whether the receipt interior may be shown. I have spent enough years ringing a bell for others to know how easily a familiar voice can drown them out. Today my offer ends with this afternoon's work and witnessing. I want you to have a place to enter, a place to stop, and room to change direction. If the answer waits, we still eat supper and keep tomorrow's crossing working.

ring_road_terms_choice.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_terms_choice.text: I would like a moment before we pack. You can help me phrase the limits aloud, because a phrase sometimes sounds different once another person hears it. Or you can mend your torn sleeve while I write the limits myself, and we will compare the page afterward. I am offering both. Quiet company is useful company too. Lan will read the final note in either case. This is preparation for an ordinary conversation, not a test you pass by persuading me to reveal more. Choose the work that will let you bring my actual words back clearly.

choices.text: Mend your sleeve while Wei Jin writes his limits.

ring_road_terms_questions.speaker: narrator
ring_road_terms_questions.text: Lin Yue asks what may be read now, what may be copied, and what he wants reserved for the common room. He answers one question at a time. The old permit may be examined; its alias, number, marks, and damage may be drawn. His offered repair recollection may be reported with its limits. The receipt cover's exterior may be copied once he presents it. Its contents wait. The echo waits. Lan repeats the list and he approves her repetition. Hearing the boundaries in another voice helps him find a missing detail: he wants the original objects returned after comparison.

ring_road_terms_silence.speaker: narrator
ring_road_terms_silence.text: Lin Yue threads a needle with her uninjured hand and closes the tear in her sleeve. Across the table, Wei Jin writes slowly on a clean strip of paper. Each time his fingers shake, he rests the brush instead of pressing harder. Su Lan reads the finished limits while he watches her face. The permit, wrapping, and exterior cover mark may be compared; the interior waits, and the echo stays sealed. He adds that the originals come home with him. Lin Yue copies the approved list after stowing her needle, grateful for the space silence left in his own sentences.

ring_road_lantern.speaker: narrator
ring_road_lantern.text: Wei Jin lifts the closed receipt cover by its edges and turns it toward the window. A small R-3 is written on the outer face, with a faded line beneath it where the cord has rubbed. Lin Yue draws the visible mark and records that she has not opened the cover. The cord remains tied throughout. Wei Jin then slips it into its inner sleeve. Afternoon light shines through the thin oilcloth, showing only a square shadow. She resists tracing that shadow as evidence. It tells her there is paper inside, and nothing about what the paper says.

ring_road_recognition_offer.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_recognition_offer.text: At the common meeting I will offer recognition against the sources actually brought there. I will say that Jin of the Lower Reed was my working alias and that I held LR-6. I will bring this closed cover so I can decide whether to show its contents in the private room. If somebody asks to inspect the ring's outside for identity, they must explain the proposed comparison before I answer. Today's examination of my own tools gives no permission for that later act. I want the question asked while I can hear it, not slipped beneath an earlier yes.

ring_road_playback_boundary.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_playback_boundary.text: And any playback gets its own question, after identity is established. You can accept an exterior comparison while declining to let anyone hear the echo. You can receive a sealed case and choose no audience. You can also ask to pause before either decision. I will carry that distinction to the meeting with the drawings. The Eel cannot search your present thoughts to test whether you remember a sound correctly, and nobody should request such a test. We need records and offered words. Your mind is already here with you, entitled to remain outside the exhibit table.

ring_road_packet.speaker: narrator
ring_road_packet.text: They wrap the drawings in dry paper and place the approved limits on top. The packet contains a permit sketch marked LR-6, the old alias in Wei Jin's words, his bounded repair account, a demonstrated seam, and the closed cover's offered exterior R-3. It contains no receipt interior and no echo playback. Wei Jin keeps the original objects in his roll. Lan signs as a witness to today's offering and copying, adding no claim about the unseen sources. Lin Yue writes her own name beneath the observation notes. Each signature has a job small enough for its signer to understand.

ring_road_return.speaker: narrator
ring_road_return.text: The three leave the ticket house by the high road. Wei Jin carries his tools; Lin Yue carries the packet. Su Lan stops at the turning to hang the changed route notice beneath a clear strip of oiled cloth. Its first line tells travelers the lower approach remains closed. The next gives the public landing and the time of the additional cart turns. Nothing in it mentions a ring. Before they continue, a man with an empty handcart reads the notice and turns at once toward the longer road, saving himself the descent they have already made.

ring_road_downstream.speaker: narrator
ring_road_downstream.text: From the high road, Lin Yue can see the freed willow caught beyond the working passage. Its branches are bright with scraps of old reed. A cart moves along the upper track, collecting the covered salt baskets under the ticket-house arrangement. Below it, the abandoned platform has become a new shape in the water. Su Lan pauses to finish the sketch Wei Jin will give his daughter. He waits without urging her on. The ruined stones had stood through much of his working life. Their failure does not erase earlier crossings, but it ends their claim on anyone's next footstep.

ring_road_hands_recovery.speaker: narrator
ring_road_hands_recovery.text: Wei Jin shifts his roll to the other hand. Lin Yue offers to carry it, and he accepts after checking the inner sleeve's tie. The little transfer is easier than the long conversation that preceded it. No confidence changes owners with the weight of the tools. He walks beside her empty-handed, flexing fingers that have begun to stiffen. Su Lan slows their pace where the slope grows steep. A cloud crosses the sun, and all three reach for their outer collars. The weather makes its ordinary claim on them while the packet waits dry beneath Lin Yue's sash.

ring_road_notice.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_notice.text: Tomorrow I will ask the crews to review the debris position, the damaged posts, and the approach closure. They can collect estimates after the first public crossing, before promising a repair date. Lan's sketch belongs with Xiu's new soundings, and the damaged rope receipt belongs in the cost account. I will ask the carrier to record how many baskets used the additional cart turns. That shows whose journey the closure has changed. None of it can tell us who owns a ring, but it gives the crews something solid to judge when they decide what this road needs next.

ring_road_public_alias.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_public_alias.text: If the old charter connection is corrected, I would like the line to show both names. Jin of the Lower Reed was a useful working name. Wei Jin is the name I use when I ask my daughter whether there is rice left in the pot. A clerk should not have to choose one of those lives in order to make the other searchable. I am willing to say that much in public. I have not offered the story of every passenger I carried, and the restored line must not imply that their confidences came ashore with mine.

ring_road_identity_caution.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_identity_caution.text: I will bring that request, and I will bring the uncertainty with it. LR-6 can connect a permit to a permitted record if the marks agree. R-3 can connect your closed cover to another record if its offered contents support the link. The shared repair seam can support an account of handling, while remaining a technique others could use. I have examined only your offered sources. Before anyone names the third owner, we need the other investigators to present theirs and explain what their observations allow. Even a fit must leave room for a mismatch we have not yet seen.

ring_road_owned_words.speaker: wei_jin
ring_road_owned_words.text: You may say I hope it is mine. I would rather that hope be present than have everyone pretend this is an exercise with no person inside it. I would like to know where the copy has waited and whether the spirit has borne work because the clerk's line went silent. If it is another person's ring, my cover still deserves its own answer and the other owner deserves theirs. Nobody abandoned a confidence by failing to arrive at a vanished stair. There may have been a road we had not found, or a letter that never reached its reader.

ring_road_common_room.speaker: narrator
ring_road_common_room.text: The high-bank boathouse stands open above the landing. Inside, separate tables wait for the investigators' packets, leaving a clear path to the sheltered side room. Lin Yue sets hers on the road table with the approved limits uppermost. Wei Jin takes his tool roll back before sitting. The permit and tied receipt cover stay with him. He studies the empty places reserved for the archive and marsh findings. Lin Yue has learned enough to recognize the temptation in their emptiness: a story could fill them easily. Evidence must arrive in the hands of the people who actually gathered it.

ring_road_daughter_arrival.speaker: narrator
ring_road_daughter_arrival.text: When the marsh team returns, Wei Xiu chooses a seat beside her father with room to stand without asking others to move. She keeps her findings for the shared report and receives the sketch of the changed approach. As he lifts his cup, her hand starts toward it, then stops; he has it securely. Lin Yue sees that restraint and remembers Su Lan's promise to accompany without answering for him. The bandage beneath Lin Yue's sleeve pulls as she sits. Her own body offers a quieter reminder that useful strength still benefits from a place to rest.

ring_road_report.speaker: lin_yue
ring_road_report.text: My road findings are ready. Wei Jin offered a permit marked LR-6, bearing the working alias Jin of the Lower Reed. He offered his own account of a retaining-loop cloth repair and demonstrated two short stitches across one long reverse fold. He presented a separately closed receipt cover for exterior inspection; I copied R-3 and left its cord tied. These sources support a hypothesis for comparison, and he retains their originals. I have heard no echo, seen no cover interior, and visited neither other investigation. Please present those findings before we decide what the combined evidence permits us to say.

ring_road_exit.speaker: narrator
ring_road_exit.text: Wei Jin rests his tool roll across his knees. The tremor in his fingers has quieted, although he keeps them clear of the cover's tie. Outside, the cart's wheels knock over the upper road stones; the afternoon's baskets are reaching their owners. Inside, the empty evidence tables begin to acquire the sounds of arriving footsteps. Lin Yue moves her packet far enough aside to give each new source its own place. Her road has brought a living ferryman to a question he is willing to face. The answer must wait for what the other roads have actually brought home.
